claims.claim: The paper reports higher SI-SNR improvement than listed baselines and generalization from two/three-speaker training to four/five-speaker tests.
claims.limitations: The evidence is synthetic WSJ0 mixtures, 8-kHz four-second windows, and a bounded count range; real rooms and end-to-end recognition are not tested. Results are author-reported.

claims.claim: The paper demonstrates both models and argues that static and dynamic versions serve different education, phonetics, pathology, and technology purposes.
claims.limitations: This is a two-page demonstration with no shared quantitative evaluation or claim of human-speech equivalence.

claims.claim: Dutch-accented English is called Dutch in 82.6% of errors in one setting; sequence-aware systems reduce this confusion while retaining mainstream performance.
claims.limitations: Datasets, accent categories, chunking, and aggregation define the result; it diagnoses a shortcut but does not prove cultural neutrality or universal transfer.

claims.claim: The authors report 13.2% relative WER improvement from pathology-aware pre-training, up to 8.7% from synthetic data, 12.2% from OOD data, and 9.7% from semantic selection.
claims.limitations: Etiologies, corpora, similarity model, and ratios bound the claim; improvements differ by condition and synthetic speech may not preserve clinical variation.

claims.claim: The paper reports gains over the baseline and competing reward objectives, with listeners preferring samples 67% of the time.
claims.limitations: The evidence uses WaveGrad 2 and selected reward predictors; predicted metrics and pairwise preference do not establish broad real-time deployment.

claims.claim: Dialogue-continuation training enables zero-shot instruction following and improves reported AQA, while AAC gains are mixed.
claims.limitations: Generated captions, benchmarks, and an LLM judge define the evidence; human usefulness for deaf or hard-of-hearing users is not established.

claims.claim: The paper reports 4%, 12%, and 34% relative EER improvements on LA, DF, and IndicTTS, with ablations separating AIED and CSD.
claims.limitations: Datasets, attacks, frozen front-end, and language coverage bound the result; IndicTTS EER remains high and no independent adversarial evaluation was performed.

claims.claim: EWC and SI keep WER more stable across ten batches and improve over ordinary sequential fine-tuning under the protocol.
claims.limitations: The protocol is simulated from MyST, uses English child speech and Whisper-small, and treats parameter importance as a proxy rather than a privacy guarantee.
